review_output: {"summary":"Review covers only the supplied source; no tools were used and the real LINE test is still NOT_RUN. These parts look correct: tenant scoping through composite (vendorId, accountId) foreign keys, OAuth pinning to an account version that is checked again inside a Serializable transaction, suppression of old queued messages after a Project switch, and the switch-versus-claim Serializable conflict. The main defect is that message deduplication keys are scoped to the vendor but not the LINE account, so messages that should go through the new account after a switch are treated as duplicates and silently dropped. Secondary findings: OAuth state is not tied to the browser that started the flow; ON DELETE RESTRICT may break tenant deletion; and the migration adds conditional unique indexes that the Prisma schema does not describe.","findings":[{"severity":"MAJOR","area":"Old-message suppression / message deduplication","file":"src/lib/line-notification.ts","issue":"Delivery deduplication keys are unique per vendor and leave out the LINE account, so a message re-queued after a Project switch is matched to the old account's suppressed row and never created for the new account.","impact":"After a switch, registration_confirmed, live_reminder and live_started messages already queued through the old account are suppressed and can never be sent through the new account.","evidence":"LineDelivery has @@unique([vendorId, idempotencyKey]), enqueue returns 'duplicate' when that key conflicts, and checkWebinarDeliverySource rebuilds the expected key without any account ID.","recommended_fix":"Add lineOfficialAccountId to the deduplication scope, either in the key itself or as @@unique([vendorId, lineOfficialAccountId, idempotencyKey]), and include it in the expected-key check.","required_test":"Queue live_reminder on account A, switch the Project to B, re-link and re-queue, then assert that A's row is suppressed and B's row is queued and sent.","confidence":0.75},{"severity":"MAJOR","area":"OAuth / login","file":"src/lib/line-login.ts","issue":"completeLineLogin accepts any valid state/code pair without checking that the callback comes from the browser that started the flow.","impact":"An attacker can send a victim a callback URL from the attacker's own flow, which links the attacker's LINE account to the victim's subject (or the reverse) or signs the victim in as the attacker.","evidence":"beginLineLogin returns only the authorization URL, and completeLineLogin({state, code}) checks only the stored stateHash, with no cookie or session-bound value.","recommended_fix":"In beginLineLogin, set an HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie tied to the state hash, and require it in completeLineLogin; for 'user' subjects, also check the current session user.","required_test":"Finishing the callback in a different browser, without the cookie set at the start, must be rejected and leave the state unconsumed.","confidence":0.5},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"Migration / tenant deletion","file":"prisma/migrations/20261016190000_project_line_accounts/migration.sql","issue":"The new foreign keys to LineOfficialAccount use ON DELETE RESTRICT, which Postgres checks immediately even while a Vendor cascade is still deleting the referencing rows.","impact":"Deleting a vendor that has projects, identities, login states or drafts can fail, depending on the order in which the cascades run.","evidence":"SalesProject, LineUserIdentity, LineLoginState and LineRichMenuDraft each reference LineOfficialAccount with ON DELETE RESTRICT, and all of them also cascade from Vendor.","recommended_fix":"Use onDelete: NoAction (ON DELETE NO ACTION) so the check runs at the end of the statement, after the vendor cascade finishes, while still blocking direct account deletion.","required_test":"Delete a Vendor that has two accounts, linked projects, identities, deliveries, login states and drafts, and assert it succeeds.","confidence":0.45},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"Migration / schema drift","file":"prisma/migrations/20261016190000_project_line_accounts/migration.sql","issue":"The migration's conditional unique indexes (LineOfficialAccount_one_default_per_vendor and LineRichMenuDraft_unbound_per_vendor) are not described in schema.prisma.","impact":"A later 'prisma migrate dev' may report drift and generate a DROP INDEX, which would silently remove the one-default-per-vendor rule that login and webhook routing depend on.","evidence":"schema.prisma only declares @@unique([vendorId, id]) on LineOfficialAccount, while the SQL creates a unique index on (vendorId) WHERE isDefault.","recommended_fix":"Describe the conditional indexes in the schema where Prisma supports it, or document them and add a CI check that the next generated migration does not drop them.","required_test":"Run prisma migrate diff against the migrated database in CI and assert that no DROP INDEX statements are produced.","confidence":0.5},{"severity":"NIT","area":"Legacy backfill / identity uniqueness","file":"prisma/migrations/20261016190000_project_line_accounts/migration.sql","issue":"LineUserIdentity.lineOfficialAccountId stays nullable after the backfill, and Postgres treats NULLs as distinct in the new unique index.","impact":"Identities from vendors with no account remain NULL; they can duplicate subjects and can never be routed or revoked through any account.","evidence":"The backfill only joins vendors that have an account; there is no NOT NULL constraint or cleanup step for the remaining rows.","recommended_fix":"Revoke or delete identities whose account is still NULL, then make the column NOT NULL (or add a CHECK constraint).","required_test":"Seed an identity for a vendor with no account, run the migration, and assert that no NULL-account identities remain active.","confidence":0.4}]}
